title: Scheduled Scrub Runner, Cross-Region Tombstone Reconciler, and Deletion Receipt Streamer
creator: Liam Chen
description: Goal: Deliver an automated scheduled "scrub runner" that enforces retention windows across geozones, reconciles tombstone records between replica sets, and emits a compact deletion receipt stream that can be exported to customer portals and audit systems. This ticket covers the PM requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and integration points with runtime batch jobs, ledger export, and customer notification endpoints. We intentionally use the term 'scrub' to differentiate this operational orchestrator from manual 'purge' tooling and to align with scheduled enforcement semantics (daily/weekly runs) rather than on-demand expunge.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler runs at configured cadence (daily by default) and launches scrub jobs for tenants with expired retention policies
Tombstone reconciler compares primary and replica tombstone sets and auto-resolves inconsistencies with retry/backoff and operator alerts
Deletion receipt stream contains cryptographic digest, timestamp, tenant id, deletion scope (user-level/object-level), and run id
Receipts are persisted for 365 days in the internal ledger and are exportable as NDJSON to the customer portal and S3-compatible buckets
End-to-end test demonstrating a tenant-configured retention expiry leading to record mark-as-deleted, tombstone propagation, and a visible receipt in the customer UI
Rollout includes a canary (5% of tenants) with monitoring for false-positives and a kill switch that prevents deletion if reconciliation failure rate > 0.5%
implementation_notes: Scheduler implemented as a new subcomponent of the retention service; reuses existing job-runner framework from ENG retention library
Scrub job performs: mark-as-deleted flag write, KV-cache invalidation, schedule async expunge for large objects, and emit tombstone message to internal topic
Reconciler runs as map-reduce across shard ranges; uses consistent hashing to pick owner replica and performs three-way compare (primary, replica A, replica B)
Receipts generated after successful tombstone confirmation; include SHA256 digest of deleted identifiers and signed using KMS key; KMS integration required (see ENG-27112)
Backpressure: job batching capped to configured token budget per tenant to avoid noisy neighbors; default cap documented in runbook
Observability: add per-run metrics (records scanned, records tombstoned, reconciliation mismatches, receipts emitted) and tracing spans for each phase
open_questions: Legal: Is the cryptographic digest and signed receipt content sufficient for GDPR/CCPA auditors, or do we need notarized timestamps?
Retention semantics: for multi-region tenants, should expiry be evaluated per-region residency policy or global earliest residency?
Export format: NDJSON vs signed ZIP package — which do downstream enterprise customers prefer for ingest?
Failure mode: if reconciler finds mismatch and operator resolution is required, do we block all deletions for that tenant or escalate and continue best-effort?
stakeholders: Engineering: Priya Desai (Retention service), Marco Ruiz (Storage shards), Joshua Park (Observability)
